assignee\\u0027s declared persona(s). Today anyone assigned a pull request gets the engineer\\u0027s PR review (code, logic, functionality). A QA persona gets a QA review: compliance and functionality through the lens of blast radius (what changed, what adjacent behavior to regression-test, what new automated end-to-end tests are owed), mostly by running the end-to-end suite locally, with the ability to launch the application locally to confirm as needed. A designer persona gets a design review: user experience, conformance to the proposed design (Figma or a working prototype), transitions and animations, CSS best practice, accessibility, look and feel, and compliance with the project\\u0027s design system if one exists, again with the ability to launch the product locally and use the feature. A team member declares zero, one, or several personas (engineer, QA, designer); no persona means the plain PR review; several personas mean every matching review runs on that assignment. All reviews for one pull request share the one worktree and branch the pr-review task already creates, but run separate agents with persona-specific prompts and criteria.\\n\\nIdea b9b09779 (review personas), piece 3 of 6: the design persona.
